text:
Anita R.: Heads up — noticing sporadic gRPC streaming stalls between pods in the new us-west-2 rack after last night's firmware push. High retransmit counts, stream stalls instead of smooth windowing.

Dave C.: Which pods/services? any pattern (same node, cross-node, same AZ)?

Anita R.: Mostly pod-to-pod across nodes on the affected rack (nodepool-gpu-3). Happens on large back-and-forth streams (chat-svc <-> model-proxy). Small unary RPCs fine.

Lucas M.: Sounds like fragmentation/PMTU issue. Did the NIC firmware change MTU/autoneg?

Anita R.: We pushed firmware v2.1.4 that adjusted default tso/gso handling. Also noticed the CNI has a VXLAN overlay with 50 byte overhead, and our host MTU is 9000 while vxlan mtu ~= 8949.

SRE Oncall: Running quick checks now. Running tracepath from model-proxy pod -> chat-svc pod:
```
$ tracepath -n 10.0.7.21
 1: 10.42.0.1 pmtu 9000
 2: 10.1.3.9 pmtu 9000
 3: 10.2.4.11 pmtu 1500
```

SRE Oncall: That looks like an unexpected drop in PMTU mid-path (host->overlay gateway).

Dave C.: Can you tcpdump on both ends and look for ICMP frag-needed? Also ddos counters?

SRE Oncall: tcpdump shows large SYN/PSH pushed but we see no ICMP frag-needed; kernel seems to be dropping large skbs after GSO offload when crossing vxlan interface. Sample:
```
09:21:33.123456 IP host1 > host2: Flags [P.], seq 1:16385, ack 1, win 65535
09:21:33.123459 IP host1 > host2: frag id 0 protocol TCP 
```

Lucas M.: Interesting — if GSO/TSO is producing big skbs that the VXLAN device doesn't accept and there's no ICMP returned (PMTU blackhole), gRPC streaming with continuous large writes can stall waiting on retransmit/acks.

Anita R.: Repro steps: send a streaming request with 16k request chunks, reproduce in ~30s. Works fine on old rack.

Dave C.: Quick mitigation: can we set net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on nodes to attempt PMTU discovery? Also try disabling GRO on vxlan interface to force fragmentation in kernel and see behavior.

SRE Oncall: Applied tcp_mtu_probing=1 on one affected node pool and toggled `ip link set dev vxlan0 gro off`. Re-ran test — streams recovered immediately, no stalls for 10+ minutes.

Anita R.: Nice. That points to a kernel offload + overlay MTU negotiation gap. Any long-term plan?

Lucas M.: Options: 1) Adjust host MTU and vxlan MTU to conservative value (e.g., host 9000 -> vxlan 8960) across fleet; 2) push NIC firmware fix to correctly expose offload capabilities; 3) disable GRO/GSO on overlay (perf hit); 4) force application to use smaller write sizes (ugly).

Dave C.: I'd prefer firmware + calibration. But as short-term, roll vxlan mtu to 1450 in the affected AZs? That will impact throughput/cost for GPU transfers.

Anita R.: We care about model weights and tensor copies between hosts — lowering MTU will raise CPU overhead and maybe double token latency. Could we rollout a targeted kernel sysctl + gro off on the specific nodepool as a stopgap?

SRE Oncall: I've prepared a canary: set `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`, `net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=0`, and `ip link set dev vxlan0 gro off` via DaemonSet for nodepool-gpu-3. Monitoring now for CPU and wire throughput.

Infra Bot: Deploy: canary-ds-mtu-fix started on nodepool-gpu-3 (pods: 3).

Dave C.: Also add an alternate route policy for heavy streaming: route by label to nodes that still have old firmware until upstream fixed.

Lucas M.: Filed infra ticket INFRA-1723 to audit MTU/autoneg across racks and NIC firmware. Will include steps to validate GSO/GRO behavior with `ethtool -k` and `ip -s link show` outputs.

Anita R.: Action items: 1) Monitor canary (SRE Oncall), 2) Pressure-test with large streaming payloads (Anita/Lucas), 3) Plan fleet-wide MTU calibration + firmware rollout (Lucas/Dave).

SRE Oncall: Canary has been 12m with no stalls so far. CPU up ~4% and p50 token latency back to normal. Rolling to remaining nodes in rack by EOD.

Anita R.: Thanks — keep me posted if anything regresses. Adding `#mtu` and `#grpc` tags to this thread. :white_check_mark:

Dave C.: When we close INFRA-1723, include automatic checks in node-up script to verify vxlan mtu vs host mtu and fail if mismatch > 200.

Lucas M.: Will do. Also looking into getting vendor patch for GSO visibility into vxlan offload path.

Anita R.: tl;dr: MTU+offload negotiation failure on new NIC firmware -> big skbs not fragmented -> no ICMP -> gRPC streaming stalls. Canary fix: enable MTU probing + disable GRO on vxlan until vendor/firmware fix or fleet MTU recalibration.
